primitives.name: Isotonic Probability Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: * * Contents: * - isotonicCalibration: non-parametric monotonic mapping (PAVA) — the gold * standard for recalibrating a monotone-but-miscalibrated score.
primitives.latex: \hat{p}_{iso}(p) = \arg\min_{q} \sum_{i} w_i (q_i - x_i)^2, \quad q_i \le q_j \text{ whenever } p_i \le p_j
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: (p, x, w) are dimensionless probabilities and binary outcomes with weights.
primitives.assumptions: The forecast scores are monotonic in the true risk, and the calibration dataset spans the full score range.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when training data has sparse coverage of extreme score regions, leading to unreliable tail estimates.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI posterior predictive checks by transforming model confidence into well-calibrated predictive probabilities. Maps to GSE by providing a monotonic utility adjustment for sequential decision-making under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on holdout samples.

primitives.name: Centered Isotonic Recalibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: * - centeredIsotonicCalibration: CIR / CenteredIsotonic — PAVA plateaus collapsed * to mass-weighted centers + linear interpolation so ranking/Kelly resolution * is preserved (distinct calibrated values ≈ sample size, not ~50 steps).
primitives.latex: \hat{p}_{CIR}(p) = \frac{\sum_{i \in B(p)} p_i x_i}{\sum_{i \in B(p)} p_i}, \quad B(p) = \{j | p_j \text{ is in the same forecast bucket as } p\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: (p_i, x_i) are forecast probability and binary outcome for sample i, and B(p) denotes the mass-weighted bucket containing p.
primitives.assumptions: The underlying isotonic fit is piecewise constant, and the centering preserves the ordering of the original scores.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when all samples share the same forecast, collapsing to a single calibrated value regardless of outcome frequency.

layer2.mapping: Extends GSI by maintaining resolution while enforcing centrality constraints, useful for conformal prediction intervals. In GSE, it enables fine-grained state transitions under uncertain observations.
layer2.telemetry: Brier Score decomposition components (reliability vs. resolution).

primitives.name: Brier Score Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: * - brierDecomposition: Murphy's reliability / resolution / uncertainty split — * the rigorous way to read WHY a Brier score is what it is.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: All terms are mean squared errors, ranging from 0 (perfect) to 1 (worst).
primitives.assumptions: The dataset is large enough to accurately estimate empirical means and variances.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Unstable when binning leads to empty cells, causing division by zero in the resolution term.

layer2.mapping: Relates to GSI's proper scoring rules as a specific instance of Bregman divergence. In GSE, it quantifies the trade-off between long-term accuracy and short-term adaptability.
layer2.telemetry: Contribution of each component to overall prediction quality.

CenteredIsotonic (PRIM-2) refines this by collapsing tied forecasts onto their mass-weighted average, reducing overfitting while retaining the ranking structure. Brier decomposition (PRIM-3) provides a fundamental disentanglement of prediction error into miscalibration (reliability), discrimination power (resolution), and inherent data variance (uncertainty). Together, these primitives form a robust toolkit for diagnosing and correcting systematic biases in probabilistic forecasts, enabling both offline evaluation and online adaptation.
